thread:
Nate: opened thread after a spike where clients retried full streaming sessions and we duplicated expensive model work. thinking: add explicit resume tokens (server-issued) to avoid blind hedging and naive retries.
Li: curious: resume token vs idempotency key? tokens are better for streaming because they encode offset and K/V cache position. idempotency keys are too coarse.
Soren: +1. resume token would let a retried client attach offset so the gateway can fast-skip already produced tokens. avoids double compute.
Keisha: big question: who issues and validates the token? edge or backend? we want minimal trust changes for model workers.
Arjun: propose edge issues an opaque resume token after first successful handshake. token maps to (route, model_version, kv_checkpoint, ttl). store token in a short-lived in-memory index with evictions. backed by redis for cross-node resume support.
Nate: storage concern: tokens proliferate if clients open many short streams. TTLs need to be small (e.g., 60s) and eviction LRU. also limit tokens per tenant.
Li: security: token should be unpredictable and HMAC-signed to avoid client forging. alternatively encode minimal info in signed JWT like `{
